- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast increase in next period to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by reducing amplitude of swings.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is bullish but price drops sharply (e.g., 5%+ drop from peak), model fails to anticipate; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast for next 3–5 days.
